prior_reason: Real defect: EN asks how a car goes backwards; BIS 'pagbalikwas sa sakyanan' means flipping/overturning, so the card reads as 'how do you flip a car over?' and then answers with reverse gear — a false picture of what reverse gear does. 'balikwas' has no dictionary entry at binisaya and zero corpus bodies outside this card; 'atras' is dictionary-listed and heavily attested.
prior_evidence: binisaya.com/cebuano/balikwas: 'No results found for the Cebuano word balikwas!' Corpus --bis balikwas = 0 bodies; 'pagbalikwas' and 'makabalikwas' = 1 body each, both this card. Independent sources gloss balikwas as 'turn suddenly to the opposite side, rise suddenly from a lying position'. binisaya.com/cebuano/atras: 'go back (v.)'. Corpus --bis atras = 7 bodies, moatras = 9, all directional-backward: ffct-02146 'pag-atras sa kamot gikan sa init' / 'yanking your hand away'; ffct-21916 'moatras ang kanyon' / 'the cannon pushes back'; dcard-01989 'pag-atras sa pusil' / 'a gun's recoil'; dcard-03322 'nag-atras' / 'moving away from each other'. The card's own terms list already carries 'gear paatras'.
previously_proposed:
Unsaon pag-atras sa sakyanan?

Ang reverse gear sa sakyanan naggamit og idler gear aron baliktaron ang pag-ikot sa wheel axle, moatras ang sakyanan!

How does a car manage to go backwards?

A car's reverse gear uses an idler gear to flip the wheel axle's rotation direction, letting the vehicle back up!
fact_bis:
Unsaon pagbalikwas sa sakyanan?

Ang reverse gear sa sakyanan naggamit og idler gear aron baliktaron ang pag-ikot sa wheel axle, makabalikwas ang sakyanan!

prior_evidence: binisaya.com/cebuano/buto: 'bang (v.); blast (v.); blow off (v.); burst (v.); explode (v.)'. Corpus --bis mobuto = 119 bodies for burst/explode (ffct-01076 'pods burst open'); 'makapabuto' = 1 body, dcard-11924, the same causative frame: 'Ang usa ka spark makapabuto sa coal dust' / 'A spark can explode coal dust'.

prior_reason: Real defect: EN 'by displacing oxygen' became 'pinaagi sa pagpalit sa oxygen' = 'by BUYING the oxygen' — palit is one of the most solidly attested words in the corpus and unambiguously means buy, so the mechanism of a CO2 extinguisher is simply not conveyed. 'puli' is dictionary-verified and the 'pag- + puli + sa + NP' frame is corpus-attested with the patient reading we need (the thing being replaced). Emphasis span 'CO2' kept verbatim.
prior_evidence: binisaya.com/cebuano/puli: 'alternate (n.); proxy (n.); substitute (n.)' — 'someone who takes the place of another'. Corpus --bis pagpalit = 18 bodies, all commerce ('not buying wild animals', 'can't afford enough nutritious food'). Corpus --bis puli = 44 bodies for replacement: ffct-01071 'puli sa maya' / 'replacing the maya'; ffct-00492 'pulihan sa 28 ... permanenteng ngipon' / 'replaced by permanent teeth'; ffct-01977 'aron pulihan ang daan ... nga selula' / 'to replace old or dead ones'. The flagged exact form 'pagpuli' = 1 body, ffct-08447 'inanay ra og pagpuli sa dahon' / 'shed just a few leaves at a time' — same pag-…-sa frame with the replaced thing as the genitive, which is the reading 'pagpuli sa oxygen' gets.
previously_proposed:

fact_en:
How do CO2 fire extinguishers put out fires?

They release CO2 to smother flames by displacing oxygen! It's super safe for electrical fires because CO2 doesn't conduct electricity.
fact_bis:
Unsaon pagpatay sa sunog sa CO2 fire extinguisher?

Naglabas kini og CO2 aron lumos sa siga pinaagi sa pagpalit sa oxygen! Luwas kini sa sunog sa kuryente kay ang CO2 dili nagdala og kuryente.

prior_reason: Two defects provable from the card's own English. (1) 'matalinghaga nga mga kilid' for 'sharp edges' — matalinghaga means figurative/metaphorical, not sharp; a child reads 'dust with metaphorical edges'. (2) 'walay hangin o tubig nga mipakin' for 'no wind or water ever smoothed it' — 'mipakin' is not a Cebuano word; the clause has no predicate, so the whole 'nothing ever smoothed it' claim is lost. The hold was only on makapahamis's rarity, and that rarity is an artefact of the inflected surface form: the root hamis is attested 140x and dictionary-confirmed, and the single hit of makapahamis is in exactly this sense. Emphasis_bis is empty; only two tokens change.
prior_evidence: ceb_usage --bis makapahamis: 1 body, ffct-08137 'Ang pag-polish sa usa ka surface makapahamis kini' / EN 'Polishing a surface makes it smoother' — identical morphology, identical sense. --bis hamis: 140 bodies, 8 titles. binisaya.com/cebuano/hamis: 'hamis (há.mis) — silky, smooth; satiny, sleek, smooth gleaming surface'. --bis hait: 236 bodies, 8 titles (e.g. ffct-00098 'hait nga bato'). Defect words self-attest only: --bis matalinghaga: 2 bodies, one of which IS ffct-33158; --bis mipakin: 1 body, which IS ffct-33158 (i.e. zero independent attestation).
previously_proposed: Ang nawong sa Moon natakpan sa regolith — crushed rock ug abug nga adunay hait nga mga kilid! Bilyun-bilyong tuig sa meteorite impact ang naghimo, ug walay hangin o tubig nga makapahamis niini.
fact_en: The Moon's surface is covered in regolith — crushed rock and dust with sharp edges! Billions of years of meteorite impacts made it, and no wind or water ever smoothed it.
fact_bis: Ang nawong sa Moon natakpan sa regolith — crushed rock ug abug nga adunay matalinghaga nga mga kilid! Bilyun-bilyong tuig sa meteorite impact ang naghimo, ug walay hangin o tubig nga mipakin.

prior_reason: Meaning-inverting defect on a SAFETY card. 'makapagligtas' = 'can rescue/save', so the Cebuano currently reads 'a fast flash flood can easily SAVE a person' — the exact opposite of the English 'can easily sweep a person off their feet', and it converts a do-not-cross warning into a reason to enter floodwater. The attestation hold on makapatumba is not a real objection: the corpus has a near-verbatim twin of this very sentence using that exact word, and the root is attested ~200x. Emphasis span 'flash flood' is present verbatim; one token changes.
prior_evidence: ceb_usage --bis makapatumba: 2 bodies — ffct-29807 'bisan mabaw lang ug paspas ang agos sa tubig-baha, makapahugno kini ug makapatumba sa usa ka tawo' / EN 'Even shallow but fast-moving floodwater ... can easily knock a person right off their feet' (same fact, same phrase 'sa usa ka tawo'); ffct-27677 'makapatumba niini' for 'make it tip over'. Roots: --bis tumba 99 bodies/12 titles, --bis matumba 100 bodies. binisaya.com/cebuano/tumba: 'to knock something over or cause it to fall; fall, tumble'. --bis makapagligtas: 1 body, which IS ffct-35224 — zero independent attestation.
previously_proposed: Ayaw pagtabok sa nabaha nga suba panahon sa ting-ulan kay ang kusog nga flash flood dali ra kaayo nga makapatumba sa usa ka tawo!
fact_en: Never cross a swollen river during the rainy season because fast-moving flash floods can easily sweep a person off their feet!
fact_bis: Ayaw pagtabok sa nabaha nga suba panahon sa ting-ulan kay ang kusog nga flash flood dali ra kaayo nga makapagligtas sa usa ka tawo!

prior_reason: Two false statements provable from the card's own English. (1) 'pinakabug-at' = 'heaviest'; English says the topsoil is the RICHEST layer. Topsoil is in fact the least dense horizon, so the Cebuano teaches a factually wrong soil-science claim, not just an odd word. (2) 'nabuak' = 'shattered/broken'; English says 'decayed' — humus comes from decay, not breakage, so the mechanism is wrong too. The pinakadato hold is closed outright by a corpus card stating this identical fact. Emphasis span 'horizons' present verbatim; two tokens change.
prior_evidence: ceb_usage --bis pinakadato: 2 bodies — ffct-02587 'Adunay mga patong ang yuta nga gitawag horizon. Ang topsoil mao ang pinakadato nga patong, puno sa sustansya' / EN 'Soil has layers called horizons. The topsoil is the richest layer, full of nutrients' — the SAME fact, already in the shipped corpus with this exact word; also ffct-02508 'pinakadato nga dagat' for 'richest marine areas'. Roots: --bis dato 157 bodies/20 titles, used figuratively throughout ('dato sa Vitamin C', 'dato sa calcium'); --bis pinaka 1730 bodies. --bis nadunot: 50 bodies/3 titles, rendering English 'rotting/decayed' (ffct-00516, ffct-00554). binisaya.com/cebuano/dato: 'opulent, rich, wealthy'.
previously_proposed:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga ang yuta adunay mga layer sama sa cake?

Ang yuta adunay mga layer nga gitawag ug horizons, ug ang topsoil mao ang pinakadato nga layer kay puno kini ug humus gikan sa mga nadunot nga tanom ug hayop.
fact_en:
Did you know soil has layers like a cake?

Soil has layers called horizons! The topsoil is the richest layer because it holds the most humus from decayed plants and animals.
fact_bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga ang yuta adunay mga layer sama sa cake?

Ang yuta adunay mga layer nga gitawag ug horizons, ug ang topsoil mao ang pinakabug-at nga layer kay puno kini ug humus gikan sa mga nabuak nga tanom ug hayop.
